body: ### Contributing guidelines - [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch ### Module(s) mini.pick ### Neovim version 0.12.x ### Description I'm having some strange behaviour when using mini.pick, mini.files and [`no-neck-pain`](https://github.com/shortcuts/no-neck-pain.nvim) together. It only happens when i invoke mini.pick while mini.files is open; where the picked file opens in the sidebuffer of no-neck-pain instead of in the center buffer, as it should. Expected: **Note**: this does NOT happen (ie. the expected behaviour happens) in the following situations: - Opening a file straight from `mini.files` when executing `nvim .` - Closing `mini.files`, then launching `mini.pick` when executing `nvim .` - Executing just `vim` without a directory, then `mini.pick` - Opening `mini.pick` from any already open buffer ### Reproduction 1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory: - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows 2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'. Populate it with the following content: ```lua vim.pack.add({ "https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim", "https://github.com/shortcuts/no-neck-pain.nvim" }) require("mini.files").setup() require("mini.pick").setup() require("no-neck-pain").setup({ width = 150, autocmds = { enableOnVimEnter = true, skipEnteringNoNeckPainBuffer = true, }, }) ``` 3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim .` (use `.` or any directory) Wait for all dependencies to install. 4. Do these interactive steps - If on a large enough screen, the `no-neck-pain` side buffers should spawn - if your screen is too small, please adjust the `width` value in the `no-neck-pain` config - The mini.files window should open - run `:lua MiniPick.builtin.files()` (WHILE `mini.files` IS OPEN!) - pick any file - the file will open on the left side buffer

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

I can reproduce and, as far as I can tell, this is an expected behavior. Pickers in 'mini.pick' have the concept of the [target window](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/1599a473aa6f5290a5d740b1144846e6f0c3963d/doc/mini-pick.txt#L868-L870), i.e. the window for which something is expected to be done by the picker. Usually it means "show file/position in that window".

As 'mini.pick' is started from the 'mini.files' floating window, *its window* is treated as a target. The way 'mini.files' works is that there is an automatic tracking of the lost focus: if the focus switched to some other window not from the explorer, the explorer is silently closed. This is usually what people expect in this situation and is aligned with how 'mini.files' explorer is expected to be used (open it, do something with it, close it).

Two facts above combined lead to this sequence: 'mini.pick' is opened thinking that 'mini.files' window is target -> 'mini.files' is closed along with target window of 'mini.pick' -> 'mini.pick' thinks that the first available "normal" window is the target (which happens to be not the one used in 'no-neck-pain.nvim').

There are several solutions here:
- Do not open 'mini.pick' directly when 'mini.files' is open. I think it is not too much to first close the explorer with a single `q` and *then* start the picker (with the proper target window).
- Adjust `config.source.choose` to ensure that the target window always comes from 'no-neck-pain.nvim'. It requires extra attention to make this 100% proof (since pickers can have their own `source.choose` defined locally), but here is the blueprint that works in the repro steps from this issue:

    ```lua
    require('mini.pick').setup({
      source = {
        choose = function(...)
          local ok, center_win_id = pcall(vim.fn.win_getid,2)
          center_win_id = ok and center_win_id or vim.fn.win_getid(1)
          MiniPick.set_picker_target_window(center_win_id)
          MiniPick.default_choose(...)
        end
      }
    })
    ```

Hope this helps.

Thanks for the detailed description and solution!

Your solution works fine when no-neck-pain is "active" but the files are not opened when no-neck-pain is not active (ie. the window is too small).

I will try to get a fix for that (checking if no-neck-pain is active somehow should suffice) and post it here if it works, to help anyone else who might need it.

Also yes, you're right that i should just close `mini.files` first, but old habits die hard

title: mini.pick && mini.files: Picked files open in the wrong buffer when `mini.files` was active when `mini.pick` was launched
